one_line_contribution: A two-environment audit that manipulates retriever recall and, separately, the availability of oracle same-binding items in the bank (nested coverage 0/0.5/1), scoring every arm as a success residual over a static prompt built from the same bank, to claim that recall above a type threshold predicts success only when the retrieved binding cannot be recovered inside the episode (flat on ALFWorld, coverage-slope on WebShop).
closest_prior_work: Verified: 2603.02473 'Diagnosing Retrieval vs. Utilization Bottlenecks in LLM Agent Memory' (verified via s2cli paper lookup; s2 2026-03-02, HF 2026-04-12) already separates the retrieval channel from the utilization channel in agent memory and concludes retrieval method dominates write strategy. It does not build a static arm from the same bank and does not manipulate duplicate availability, so it does not collide, but it weakens the proposal's framing that recall and success are 'never dissociated' in the agent literature. Verified: 2604.04949 LRAT (s2, SIGIR, 4 cits) reports evidence recall and end-to-end success jointly for retrievers trained on agent trajectories — the proposal's characterization of it is accurate. The sharper threat is the home literature the proposal never cites: 2601.17532 (IGP) states outright that retrieval relevance metrics such as NDCG correlate weakly with end-to-end QA quality and can turn negative under multi-passage injection, 2512.20854 asks the same about recall, and 2604.08920 ('Beyond Relevance: Utility-Centric Retrieval in the LLM Era') is a survey of exactly this premise; all three surfaced on the novelty card, all single-turn QA. Together they make the general half of the headline ('recall ranks retrievers, success does not') a known result, leaving the agentic instantiation plus the recoverability moderator as the new part. On the ALFWorld null specifically, 2412.16926 'Revisiting In-Context Learning with Long Context Language Models' and 2405.00200 (both returned by my home-vocabulary query, hf) already report that example-selection method stops mattering once enough examples are in context — the ICL-side version of P1c/P1d, uncited here. Also verified: 2505.00234 Traj-Bootstrap (NeurIPS, 19 cits), 2602.08316 SWE-ContextBench, 2605.16986 Skills on the Fly, 2607.10608 Compliance Trap, 2604.27003 'When Continual Learning Moves to Memory'. I could not individually verify 2512.20854, 2601.17532, 2508.05909, 2604.08920 by paper lookup, but all four appeared with matching titles and dates in my searches and on the novelty card; 2605.24117, 2608.20707, 2606.21249, 2506.08184 and 2603.04814 I did not verify at all.
strongest_objection: The moderator that carries the whole paper — whether the binding is recoverable inside the episode — is observed across two environments, not manipulated. ALFWorld and WebShop differ in horizon, action space, reward definition, base success rate and agent competence; if the ALFWorld slope is flat and the WebShop slope is +16, recoverability is one of a dozen explanations, and the proposal's own generalization ('recall above the type threshold is uninformative unless the bank carries non-recoverable bindings') is a claim from n=2 environments. This is precisely the criticism that sank decorative_retriever ('overlap was observed, not manipulated'), reproduced one level up: coverage is manipulated, recoverability is not. A second, more damaging problem is internal. Measurement C's +17.2 was measured with the retrieval arm and static3 drawing on the same expert pool (A's bank is the expert bank, C is paired with A), so it is already a per-episode-selection effect at fixed source. P1c then asks a no-selection arm (three fixed bank medoids per type) to close that same gap, which requires the expert-to-self source swap to be worth about +17 net — larger than static3 minus k0 (+12.4) and larger than the entire retrieval gain the paper is explaining. The proposal never argues for a source effect of that size, never states the implied and counterintuitive claim (the agent's own trajectories are far better in context than expert demonstrations of the same type), and if E0's bank supplementation means the new BM25 arm draws from a different pool than C's did, then P1b is not the replication it is billed as. Third, two of the five prediction families do not carry their stated weight: P3b is an accounting identity (BM25 gain = product recall x oracle effect, with both sides estimated from the same S cells and the same treatment, at a +/-8 tolerance wider than the +5 to +10 value it predicts at b_ws = 0.3-0.5), and P4, the 'headline cross-environment slope', reduces on an equally spaced 0/0.5/1 grid to the c=1 minus c=0 endpoint difference already scored by P2 and P3a, so it is an algebraic restatement presented as an independent test with its own MDE.
what_would_fix_it: (1) Manipulate recoverability within one environment instead of inferring it across two: on ALFWorld, run a non-recoverable variant (randomize receptacle contents between the bank episode and the test episode, or disable the free look/examine that makes object location cheap) and show the coverage slope turns on; on WebShop, run a recoverable variant (give the agent an oracle attribute-to-product lookup) and show it turns off. A within-environment sign flip is the experiment that would actually license the rule; the cross-environment contrast is then confirmation, not evidence. (2) Add a binding-redacted control on WebShop (same-product trajectory present, product identity and asin masked, length and format matched) so that 'coverage helps' is attributable to the binding rather than to relevance or trajectory quality in general. (3) Fix P1c by running BM25 restricted to the expert pool on the same fresh seeds as static3 and static3-bank, so the source contrast and the selection contrast are measured within one study rather than against C. (4) State the ALFWorld nulls as equivalence tests (TOST at the +/-8 bound) rather than point estimates inside a band, since the entire ALFWorld half is a null and a point estimate of +7 with CI [+2,+12] would 'confirm' it. (5) Drop P3b or rebuild it as the entailment check suggests (rank-matched oracle arm, b_ws and the oracle effect estimated on disjoint seeds, tolerance as a fraction of the predicted value). (6) Either add an unequally spaced coverage rung so P4 is not the endpoint difference, or stop billing P4 as the headline and report P2/P3a as the primary contrasts with P4 as a summary statistic.
missing_baseline: A binding-redacted WebShop arm: the same-product trajectory retained at rank 1 with the product identity (name, asin, the attribute-satisfying option choices) masked, token- and format-matched. Without it, the +16 coverage effect on S is consistent with 'we planted a highly relevant, high-quality trajectory' and cannot be attributed to the non-recoverable binding, which is the paper's whole mechanism. Secondarily, a BM25-over-the-expert-pool arm on the fresh seeds, which is the only way to separate the claimed exemplar-source effect from per-episode selection within one study rather than by comparing against Measurement C's differently-banked numbers.
preprint_collision: No verified collision. All searches below used channel (a), the s2cli literature command (s2 + hf); WebSearch was unavailable in this session and was not used. Queries: (1) 'retriever recall does not predict agent task success dissociation experience memory' (no recency) — returned 2608.07169, 2607.10608, 2606.24595, 2605.29463, 2601.09503 (Task2Quiz: task success is a poor indicator of environment understanding), none manipulating duplicate availability or scoring against a static arm; (2) 'near-duplicate trajectory in memory bank drives retrieval gain agent benchmark leakage' --recent — empty; (3) 'duplicate experience in memory bank retrieval gain agent' --recent — 2607.28272 MemHarness, 2604.27003, 2604.20572, 2606.22844, 2608.00017, no collision; (4) 'retrieved exemplars versus fixed exemplars control ALFWorld WebShop agent memory static prompt baseline' — empty; (5) home-vocabulary, no agent/memory words, 'retrieved demonstrations versus random demonstrations in-context example selection matters' — 2412.16926, 2405.00200, 2202.12837, 2305.04320, 2506.04579, which is where the uncited ICL threat to the ALFWorld null lives; (6) 'coverage of similar past tasks predicts memory benefit LLM agent' --recent — nothing on point; (7) 'retrieval quality metrics versus downstream task success agent memory oracle retrieval upper bound' --recent — 2603.02473, 2604.08920, 2512.20854, 2604.04949; (8) 'planted oracle same-task trajectory in bank ablation shows memory gain comes from task overlap not generalization' — nothing on point; (9) 'when is retrieval necessary environment property manipulation two levels agent memory ablation static prompt' --recent — 2607.20972, 2606.04315, 2603.02473; (10) closest named method, 'self-generated in-context examples database agent ALFWorld WebShop' — 2505.00234 (verified, NeurIPS, 19 cits), plus TRAD 2403.06221 and Learn-by-interact 2501.10893, neither with a static or random control. Judging the proposal's own check: it is well above average for this round — four query classes, IDs attached to every hit, one --recent mechanism query, one home-vocabulary query, and one paper lookup actually performed (2505.00234, which I independently confirmed is the Traj-Bootstrap paper). Two real gaps. First, its 'home' query stayed inside RAG-QA correlation studies and missed the utility-based retrieval literature that owns the general claim (2504.00573, 2503.01478 SePer, 2404.13781, 2604.08920), all of which the automated novelty card surfaced and none of which appear in Related Work; a proposal whose headline is 'relevance metrics do not predict downstream utility' cannot omit the subfield named after that observation. Second, it ran no query in the in-context-learning vocabulary about example-selection sensitivity, which is where 2412.16926 and 2405.00200 sit and where the ALFWorld null is closest to being already known. Neither is a collision, but both mean the novelty argument is narrower than the check asserts.
